提供端到端可运行示例

candidates.reason: Python 生态中知名度很高的 AI 浏览器代理库，直接面向让 Agent 操作浏览器完成任务；值得进一步检查其 Playwright/浏览器驱动、端到端示例、模型配置方式以及工具调用可观测性。
专注于用 AI 自动化浏览器工作流，和“通过浏览器完成实际任务”的目标高度相关；值得查看是否有可运行的端到端示例、模型配置说明以及动作执行过程展示。
面向真实世界任务自动化的多智能体项目，可能包含浏览器操作能力和完整任务示例；适合进一步分析其 Agent 编排、浏览器工具接入与模型配置。
提供 Web 任务自动化的 Gym 环境，适合学习和复现可重复的浏览器任务；值得检查其与 Playwright/浏览器自动化的集成方式以及是否便于观察 Agent 动作。
结合 CDP 与 CodeAgent 架构，让 LLM 编写并执行 Python 代码来操作网页；值得深入查看其浏览器自动化实现、示例流程和工具调用过程是否可观察。
小型但聚焦的 Web Agent 项目，使用可访问性树规划浏览器操作；值得检查其是否提供可运行示例、Playwright 类工具接入和模型配置说明。
开源的 MCP 原生浏览器 Agent，强调给 AI Agent 真实浏览器并保留人类介入；适合进一步分析其浏览器控制方式、端到端演示和模型/工具配置。
定位为让 AI Agent 浏览、读取并交互网页的智能浏览器工具；值得检查其是否包含完整 Agent 循环、可运行示例以及浏览器自动化底层实现。

evaluations.purpose_summary: Open-source Python library for building AI browser agents that use LLMs to drive a real browser (Playwright/CDP-based) to complete web tasks, with an optional hosted cloud offering.

must_have_checks.requirement: 使用 Playwright 或同类浏览器自动化工具
must_have_checks.evidence: Topics include 'playwright' and 'browser-automation'; README describes driving a local or cloud browser; structure contains browser_use/browser/session.py, watchdogs, and CDP-related files (cdp, chrome.py).

must_have_checks.requirement: 提供端到端可运行示例
must_have_checks.evidence: README Path 3 gives a complete install + .env + agent.py quickstart using Agent, Browser, ChatOpenAI; also actor/playground examples (flights.py, mixed_automation.py, playground.py).

must_have_checks.requirement: 包含模型配置说明
must_have_checks.evidence: README instructs adding OPENAI_API_KEY to .env and shows ChatOpenAI/ChatBrowserUse imports; .env.example present; config.py exists.

strengths: Directly targets browser-based AI agents with Playwright/CDP automation
Clear quickstart with model configuration and runnable agent.py example
Rich component structure (agent, browser, dom, controller, watchdogs) exposing end-to-end architecture
Active maintenance with recent pushes and CI workflows
MIT licensed and usable locally without mandatory SaaS
weaknesses: Very large codebase (665 entries, service.py ~165KB, beta/service.py ~256KB) which is hard to fully comprehend in an 8-hour budget
Core agent logic is monolithic and complex, reducing code clarity for learners
README is heavily marketing/cloud-oriented, mixing hosted product paths with the open-source library
Requires an LLM API key (cost/dependency) to actually run end-to-end
uncertainties: Exact depth of inline comments and internal documentation not fully visible from evidence
Whether a minimal self-contained runnable example exists beyond the README snippet
Tool-call observability (nice-to-have) is implied by demo_mode/gif but not explicitly confirmed in README

evaluations.purpose_summary: Skyvern is a Python-based AI agent system that automates browser-based workflows using LLMs and computer vision, built on top of Playwright. It provides a Playwright-compatible SDK with AI capabilities plus a no-code workflow builder, allowing agents to navigate and complete tasks on websites without hardcoded XPaths.

must_have_checks.requirement: 使用 Playwright 或同类浏览器自动化工具
must_have_checks.evidence: README explicitly states Skyvern provides a 'Playwright-compatible SDK that adds AI functionality on top of playwright' and gives agents 'the ability to interact with websites using browser automation libraries like Playwright'. Topics include 'playwright', 'puppeteer', 'selenium'.

must_have_checks.requirement: 提供端到端可运行示例
must_have_checks.evidence: README includes a Quickstart with pip install and Docker Compose options, a demo video, and a GIF showing an end-to-end workflow (geico_shu_recording). The quickstart commands (skyvern quickstart, docker compose up) provide runnable end-to-end setup.

must_have_checks.requirement: 包含模型配置说明
must_have_checks.evidence: README instructs users to 'Configure your LLM provider in .env' and copy .env.example to .env, then add an LLM API key. A .env.example file (14826 bytes) exists in the repo structure.

strengths: Directly built on Playwright with AI agent layer, matching the core topic
Clear architecture description (swarm of agents: observer/planner/actor) with system diagram
Multiple setup paths (pip and Docker Compose) with troubleshooting notes
Active maintenance: recent pushes, many workflows, large community (23k+ stars)
Explicit LLM provider configuration via .env.example
weaknesses: Very large codebase (5946 entries, 656MB) with many components (DB, alembic migrations, UI, API, SDKs) — heavy for an 8-hour learning budget
Requires database (SQLite/Postgres), Docker, and multiple services, increasing setup complexity
AGPL-3.0 license may restrict some reuse
Core agent logic is buried in a large production system, harder to isolate for learning
uncertainties: README was truncated; full model configuration details and example task definitions not fully visible
Whether a minimal single-task end-to-end example exists without full server/UI stack is unclear
Tool-call observability (nice-to-have) is implied by observer thoughts/artifacts but not explicitly confirmed in visible evidence
Actual time to get a working end-to-end run within 8 hours is uncertain given multi-component setup

evaluations.purpose_summary: OWL is a multi-agent task automation framework built on CAMEL-AI that uses browser automation (via Playwright MCP) and other toolkits to let AI agents complete real-world tasks, achieving top GAIA benchmark scores among open-source frameworks.

must_have_checks.requirement: 使用 Playwright 或同类浏览器自动化工具
must_have_checks.evidence: README includes a dedicated 'Install Playwright MCP Service' section and lists Playwright MCP as a browser toolkit; community_usecase also contains a 'Puppeteer MCP' example (a comparable browser automation tool).

must_have_checks.requirement: 提供端到端可运行示例
must_have_checks.evidence: README has a 'Quick Start' with Basic Usage and Example Tasks, plus a community_usecase directory with multiple runnable end-to-end examples (e.g., Airbnb-MCP, Puppeteer MCP demo.py, cooking-assistant run_gpt4o.py).

must_have_checks.requirement: 包含模型配置说明
must_have_checks.evidence: README has 'Setup Environment Variables' (direct env vars and .env file), a 'Running with Different Models' section with 'Model Requirements' and 'Supported Models', and a 'Customizing Your Configuration' section.

strengths: Explicit Playwright MCP integration for browser automation
Rich, well-structured README with installation options (uv, pip, conda, Docker), model config, and quick start
Multiple end-to-end community use cases demonstrating real browser/tool tasks
Active project with recent pushes, NeurIPS 2025 acceptance, and large community
Multi-agent architecture with observable toolkits and MCP support
weaknesses: Large, complex multi-agent framework may be heavy to fully understand within an 8-hour budget
Depends on external CAMEL-AI framework and MCP services (Node.js, Playwright MCP) adding setup complexity
No license declared in metadata, which is a concern for reuse
Core agent logic is partly abstracted into the CAMEL dependency, reducing transparency of internals
uncertainties: Full README was truncated; exact model configuration details and example task specifics not fully visible
Repository structure was truncated (192 entries, reposcout_truncated=true), so complete source layout is unknown
Whether a minimal single-file end-to-end browser example exists without heavy dependencies is unclear
Actual setup time and dependency friction for an intermediate learner within 8 hours is uncertain

evaluations.purpose_summary: BrowserGym is a Gymnasium-based framework/environment for web task automation, providing a unified interface for LLM web agents to interact with browsers across multiple benchmarks (MiniWoB, WebArena, WorkArena, etc.). It is a research framework rather than a ready-to-run end-user agent.

must_have_checks.requirement: 使用 Playwright 或同类浏览器自动化工具
must_have_checks.evidence: README setup instructs `playwright install chromium`; core module contains browser env/action/observation code (env.py, action/functions.py, javascript/ frame scripts) consistent with Playwright-based automation.

must_have_checks.requirement: 提供端到端可运行示例
must_have_checks.evidence: README provides a boilerplate env<>agent loop with `action = ...  # implement your agent here`, i.e. the agent itself is left to the user. No complete runnable agent example is shown in the README; the demo is a video. Full end-to-end agent examples may live in the separate AgentLab repo.

must_have_checks.requirement: 包含模型配置说明
must_have_checks.evidence: README does not document LLM/model configuration (API keys, model selection). The framework is model-agnostic and the agent is user-implemented; model config likely resides in AgentLab, which is not part of this evidence.

strengths: Well-structured modular monorepo (core, experiments, per-benchmark packages) with clear separation of env, action, observation, task
Explicitly built on Playwright with browser automation primitives
Rich benchmark ecosystem and Gymnasium-compatible interface aids understanding of web-agent environments
Active maintenance: recent pushes, CI workflows, tests, PyPI packaging
weaknesses: Not a ready-to-run agent: README leaves the agent loop as `action = ...` placeholder, so end-to-end runnable example is not demonstrated
No model/LLM configuration guidance in README
Many benchmarks require heavy external setup (WebArena, WorkArena, Google Cloud for Knows), increasing reproduction cost
Framework/research orientation rather than a task-completing consumer agent
uncertainties: Whether a complete runnable agent example exists elsewhere in the repo (e.g., experiments/loop.py) is not confirmed by evidence
Model configuration may be documented in AgentLab or sub-READMEs not included in evidence
Actual setup complexity and time to reproduce within 8 hours is unclear given per-benchmark dependencies

evaluations.purpose_summary: OpenBrowser is a Python framework for AI-driven browser automation that combines direct Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) communication with a CodeAgent architecture, where an LLM writes Python code executed in a persistent namespace to navigate, interact with, and extract information from web pages autonomously.

must_have_checks.requirement: 使用 Playwright 或同类浏览器自动化工具
must_have_checks.evidence: README states the project uses 'Raw CDP Communication - Direct Chrome DevTools Protocol' and benchmarks include stats_playwright.json, indicating it is a browser automation tool of the same class as Playwright (CDP-based).

must_have_checks.requirement: 提供端到端可运行示例
must_have_checks.evidence: README Quick Start shows a runnable Python example using CodeAgent with a task ('Go to google.com and search...'), and the repo contains benchmarks/e2e_codeagent_test.py, e2e_llm_benchmark.py, and e2e_published_test.py as end-to-end examples.

must_have_checks.requirement: 包含模型配置说明
must_have_checks.evidence: README has a 'Configuration' section and 'Supported LLM Providers' listing 15 providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, AWS Bedrock, Azure, Ollama, etc.), plus optional dependency installs per provider and backend/env.example.

strengths: Clear CodeAgent architecture where the LLM writes Python executed in a persistent namespace, exposing meaningful Agent concepts
Extensive documentation: full docs site, docs/customize sections for agent, browser, tools, hooks, and code-agent
Multiple end-to-end runnable examples and benchmarks in the repo
Broad LLM provider support with explicit configuration guidance
MIT licensed and actively maintained with CI workflows and tests
weaknesses: Uses raw CDP rather than Playwright directly, so learners expecting Playwright APIs may need to adapt
Large repository (~1032 entries) with a substantial backend (FastAPI, VNC, WebSocket, kiosk) that adds complexity beyond the core agent
Hosted cloud dashboard is promoted, though core functionality appears usable locally
README is long and mixes many integration modes (MCP, CLI daemon, plugins), which can obscure the core learning path
uncertainties: Whether the core agent can be fully reproduced within an 8-hour budget given the backend/VNC components
Exact setup friction for the persistent-namespace code execution environment is not fully detailed in the provided README excerpt
Whether tool-call observation is exposed in a simple local mode (nice-to-have) is not confirmed from evidence

Includes runnable examples, instruction files, and a complete sample run report with step screenshots for observing behavior
MIT licensed, Python 3.10+, with CI workflow, pre-commit config, and packaging via pyproject.toml

Selector-learning and WebSocket realtime features add dependencies and moving parts beyond a minimal browser agent

top_repositories.recommendation_reason: OWL is the strongest match for learning browser-based AI agents because it explicitly integrates Playwright MCP, documents model configuration, and provides Quick Start plus multiple end-to-end community examples. Its documentation quality, maintenance health, and direct Playwright evidence outweigh its heavier framework complexity for an intermediate learner.
tradeoffs: The multi-agent framework is large and partly depends on external CAMEL-AI abstractions, which may reduce transparency when tracing core agent logic.
Setup involves Playwright MCP and Node.js-related dependencies, adding friction within an 8-hour learning budget.
No license is declared in the supplied metadata, which is a reuse concern.
The repository structure was truncated in the evaluation data, so the full source layout and presence of a minimal single-file browser-agent example are uncertain.

Follow the environment variable and model configuration sections to connect a supported model before attempting browser tasks.

Review the tradeoffs between multi-agent orchestration and simpler single-agent browser loops, and note what would be needed for a minimal reproduction.

tradeoffs: Browser automation is based on raw Chrome DevTools Protocol rather than Playwright APIs, so learners expecting Playwright patterns must translate concepts.

The hosted cloud dashboard is promoted, although core functionality appears locally usable.

ranking.final_reason: All three repositories satisfy the must-have requirements, but OWL remains the best choice because it has the highest deterministic score and the clearest explicit Playwright MCP integration, strong documentation for model setup, multiple end-to-end examples, and better maintenance health than the alternatives. OpenBrowser is technically close but relies on raw CDP and a larger backend, while Clawome uses Playwright directly but has lower maintenance health and a more complex browser-agent implementation. OWL provides the best balance for an intermediate learner who wants to study and reproduce a browser-capable AI agent within an 8-hour budget.
